subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw enforce automatic sensitive-value sanitization on final user-visible agent output in core, route it to a plugin using outbound hooks, or explicitly keep core limited to the current log/transcript/tool redaction boundaries?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested behavior changes a security boundary, user-visible content, and likely config surface, so automation should not choose the permanent policy.

options.title: Approve a narrow core sanitizer
options.body: Add an explicit core output-sanitization boundary with safe defaults, schema/help/docs, focused tests, and reuse of existing redaction helpers rather than a parallel pattern engine.

options.title: Route to plugin ownership
options.body: Use reply_payload_sending or message_sending hooks for an optional sanitizer plugin if maintainers want core to stay lean and keep this capability outside bundled defaults.

options.title: Keep current boundaries
options.body: Document that core supports log, transcript, diagnostic, and tool-payload redaction but does not rewrite final assistant output unless a separate security design is approved.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core sanitizer
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core output-sanitization boundary with safe defaults, schema/help/docs, focused tests, and reuse of existing redaction helpers rather than a parallel pattern engine.

likelyOwner.reason: This group owns security-sensitive config and secret-handling review paths in CODEOWNERS.
